readings: Compute each film rating's average length, ignoring NULL lengths. Take the baseline as the average length over all films, with each film counting equally. Keep the ratings whose average length is above the baseline. Let M be the unweighted mean of those kept ratings' average lengths. Keep only the ratings whose average length is above M. Return one row with three values: (1) the mean of the remaining ratings' average lengths; (2) the mean of (rating average minus baseline) over the remaining ratings; (3) the mean of (rating average minus M) over the remaining ratings, where M is the step-1 mean computed before the second filter. Do not round anything.

Compute each film rating's average length, ignoring NULL lengths. Take the baseline as the average length over all films, with each film counting equally. Keep the ratings whose average length is above the baseline. Take the unweighted mean of those ratings' average lengths and keep only the ratings whose average length is above that mean. Return one row with three values: (1) the mean of the final remaining ratings' average lengths, called F; (2) the mean of (rating average minus baseline) over the final remaining ratings; (3) the mean of (rating average minus F) over the final remaining ratings, where F is the mean of the final remaining ratings only. Do not round anything.
